51503198.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to MAGEA4 (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21-(DE3) by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Results Section - ITC Measurements: The affinity of each peptide for full length MAGE-A4 was assessed by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), which confirms tight binding with each peptide displaying low nanomolar K_D values (Figure 1E and Supporting Information, Figure S1). We next tested whether this binding is localized to the highly conserved MHD or the N-terminal region of MAGE-A4. ITC against purified MAGE-A4-MHD confirms the MHD as the key binding locus for all three peptides, suggesting that these macrocycles might be capable of inhibiting the interaction between MAGE-A4 and RAD18.
original_paragraph.Figure 1E Caption: Table reporting the ITC measured K_D values and TR-FRET A measured IC_50 values for each synthesized peptide.
original_paragraph.Supporting Information S1: The ITC experiments were performed using a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Panalytical). MAGE-A4 or MAGE-A4-MHD (10–20 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the peptide (100–200 μM) was loaded into the syringe. The experiments were conducted at 25 °C with 20 injections of 2 μL each, spaced 120 s apart. The data were analyzed using Origin software (Malvern Panalytical) with a one-site binding model. The buffer used was 20 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, and 0.02% NaN3. A blank experiment with buffer in the syringe was performed to correct for heat of dilution.

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, 0.02% NaN3
assay_conditions.control_method: A blank experiment with buffer in the syringe was performed to correct for heat of dilution.
